summary: Dagmar Schwerk specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg from around 2012 to 2017 and held a professorship at the University of Leipzig around 2022.

Taichi Tado is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology. In 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Daiei Kaneko (1881–1976) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1899–1903) and under Manshi Kiyozawa (~1901–1903). He taught at Otani University (~1916–1928) and Toyo University (~1928–1944), and founded Koho Gakuen.
Daigo Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2006, he was affiliated with Ryukoku University as a research student (研究生).

Daijaku Judith Kinst works in Buddhist and religious studies. She served on the faculty at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) and as Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Daijo Tokiwa (1870–1945) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora, he held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1925–1931) and Toyo University (1931).

Daiki Sasaki (born 1977) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1996–2005). He later taught there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015) and instructor (~2016), and served as a full-time lecturer at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2015).

Dainin Katagiri (1928–1990) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Eihei-ji and Komazawa University, served as a priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission, became interim abbot at San Francisco Zen Center (1984–1985), and founded Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.

Dairyu Michael Wenger (born 1947) studied at The New School and under Sojun Mel Weitsman. A Buddhist studies scholar, he served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center (~1984–1992) and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center.

Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki (1870–1966) was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology scholar. Educated at Waseda and the University of Tokyo, he held major academic posts at Gakushuin University, Otani University, and Columbia University.

Daishun Ueyama (1934–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He spent his career at Ryukoku University as assistant professor (~1970–1978), professor (~1978–2003), and president (~1996–2000).

Daito Shimaji (1875–1927) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku and Otani universities, he taught at Toyo University (~1903–1927), Rissho University (~1904–1927), Komazawa University (~1906–1927), and the University of Tokyo (1923).

Daiun Sogaku Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University, studying under numerous teachers including Dokutan Sōsan, and served as a professor at Komazawa University from 1911 to 1923.

Dale S. Wright (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, W. Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann, and was appointed Gamble Professor at Occidental College around 1980.

Dalsukh Malvania (1910–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1948–1959), Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, the University of Toronto, and served as Director of the L. D. Institute of Indology (~1963–1973).
Damchö Gyatso studied under Penor Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown (born 1951) is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford, and served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London, beginning in 1995.

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi (1907–1966) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Harvard University under George David Birkhoff, he held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962).

Dan Arnold (born 1965) specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Carleton College, Columbia, Iliff, and the University of Chicago, he held posts at McGill University and the University of Chicago (2004–2011).
